subject: Intermittent silent packets from Willowbrook on-prem gateway
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@willowbrook.health>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: periodic silent packets to Redwood inference private endpoint

Hi Logan,

We're seeing intermittent "silent" TCP connections to the private inference endpoint (10.44.12.7) from our on-prem cluster. App logs show requests sent but no response for ~200–500ms before connection recovers; sometimes the connection resets. Issue started after we rotated the edge NAT gateway config late last night.

Attached: quick pcap capture and a traceroute sample. Key observations from our side:
- A few flows show SYN/ACK but then no payloads for tens of packets; retransmits happen.
- Traceroute shows ECMP across two transit peers; one path has a hop where latency jumps and then packets drop.

Can you confirm whether Redwood private gateway saw anything abnormal? We need help triaging routing asymmetry and whether NAT or SG is interfering.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Monroe
Infrastructure Lead — Willowbrook Health

Attachments: willowbrook-pcap-20270530.tar.gz, traceroute-willowbrook-20270530.txt

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@willowbrook.health>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: periodic silent packets to Redwood inference private endpoint

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the captures. Looping in Evelyn, Mina and Diego from networking.

Immediate asks:
- Mina: can you pull the conntrack / NAT stats for the RED-GW that handles Willowbrook (seen as src 203.0.113.x on our side)? Look for conntrack drops/reuse and NAT port exhaustion.
- Diego: can you check the routing hash for the peer ASes and whether any ECMP weighting changed after last night's config?
- Evelyn: if this is an MTU/fragmentation issue, can we validate if any of the intermediate hops are doing MSS clamp or dropping fragments?

Alex — we'll keep you posted; if you can also include a sample tcpdump with the 3-way handshake + 1st data packets that would help.

— Logan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: periodic silent packets to Redwood inference private endpoint

Quick triage notes after initial look at the pcap and our gateway metrics:
- Conntrack: spikes in "INVALID" followed by immediate DROP for a subset of Willowbrook source IPs around 02:45–03:10 UTC. Counts rolled back after manual conntrack cleanup.
- NAT: observed reuse of ephemeral ports for flows from the same source IP when conntrack entries aged out prematurely (conntrack timeout at ~30s for established flows looks low).
- MTU: no obvious ICMP frag-needed messages in the pcap, but I see TCP segments with MSS 1460 and some fragmentation suspicion where MSS negotiation is absent (likely from 3rd-party firewall).
- Security groups: our SG logs show no explicit DENY for those flows.

Hypothesis: asymmetric path + short conntrack timeout at RED-GW causing sessions to flip to different NAT mapping (different backend) while Willowbrook retransmits -> apparent silence. Possible contributor: middlebox rewriting TTL/seq or dropping fragments.

Next steps: 1) Pull full conntrack dump and increase established timeout to 300s temporarily; 2) Ask Willowbrook to confirm no mid-path firewall performing MSS clamp (or to enable icmp frag-needed).

I'm going to run tcpdump on the RED-GW with direction and port filters and capture full handshakes. Attaching a short excerpt: routing-table-before-after.txt (showing no route change on our side).

— Mina
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@willowbrook.health>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: periodic silent packets to Redwood inference private endpoint

More data from the edge NAT and BGP view:
- BGP: both transit peers are up; last night's policy change introduced a new community that adjusted MED on peer B (the less-preferred path). That change caused an ECMP imbalance: ~85% of Willowbrook flows land on peer A, ~15% on peer B.
- NAT mapping: when flows exit via peer B, the SNAT uses a different pool (SNAT-B) with different ephemeral port ranges. I see flows that start via SNAT-A but subsequent retransmits hit SNAT-B mapping (asymmetric). The backends drop packets for mismatched source-port mapping — server side enforces strict expected 4-tuple.
- I also noticed conntrack entries timing out due to our expedited garbage collection job (cron) that runs every 30s and aggressively flushes entries that look idle. That job ran during the initial incident window.

Proposed immediate remediation (low-risk):
1) Pause/disable the aggressive conntrack GC for the RED-GW for 1 hour.
2) Temporarily expand SNAT port pools for SNAT-B to match SNAT-A.
3) Work with Willowbrook to pin their outbound flows (source IP consistency) or short-lived BGP policy rollback to remove the MED change on peer B so traffic is not split.

I'll open NWK-8124 to track and attach config snippets. If we do 1+2 now we should see sessions stabilize.

— Diego
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@willowbrook.health>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Oncall Cloud Ops <oncall-cloud@partnerops.io>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: periodic silent packets to Redwood inference private endpoint

Alex — we applied immediate mitigations: paused conntrack GC and widened SNAT-B ephemeral range. We're also recommending Willowbrook roll back the MED change or pin to a single egress. Please monitor for recurrence; we expect reduced silent windows.

Oncall Cloud Ops, if you see any downstream provider flapping, please chime in.

Thanks,
Logan

From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@willowbrook.health>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: periodic silent packets to Redwood inference private endpoint

Logan / team — confirmation: after your changes traffic stabilized overnight. No silent windows observed in the 12-hour window post-change. Willowbrook also removed the MED tweak on peer B and will keep source IPs consistent for the next 72 hours while we monitor.

We appreciate the quick turnaround. Please leave the conntrack timeout at the relaxed setting for 24 hours and then we can schedule a controlled test for the aggressive GC to validate behavior.

Alex
(thread archived; JIRA NWK-8124 created, artifacts uploaded to Drive link in metadata)
